INCIDENT - At 01:20Z OPO AN contacted the Chief Controller and requested that JG NC, DEP 01:10Z, MIS 15F34, head toward Anápolis, because control (TABA) was detecting some unidentified plots near the Base on the TA-10.
JG NG began monitoring TABA at 01:28Z and attempted reconnaissance, managing to see lights, but nothing was identified.
Some of these plots were also initialized by COpM, at low speed and with quality factor 6.
At 02:40Z, on JG AM's DEP, COpM requested an attempt to contact a plot common to COpM's and TABA's sweeps. JG AM obtained contact for 2 sweeps of its radar at 03NM and 01NM, then lost it.
At 04:34Z reconnaissance was attempted again. This time the ACFT (negro 2) reported on COpM's frequency that it had seen a flashing light at 09NM. It was ordered to head toward the target. Negro 2 lost visual contact with the light and was instructed to land with TABA. On TABA's frequency, negro2 saw an unidentified object on final approach to runway 06, over the NAB. The object headed toward the "Pandorga" Sector and then took heading 060°. After this, negro 2 was instructed to land.

No dia 05 MAI, por volta das 2205P, TABA informou que estava detetando alguma coisa que se deslocava entre as radiais 120 e 270 de Anápolis, com proa aproximada 270, afastado de Anápolis de 3 a 12 MN, dependendo da radial que estivesse cruzando e que quando tal objeto cruzou a final da pista 06, foi detetado pelo PAR e que, graças a isso, pode ser verificado que ele estava a uma altitude de 6150 pés.
Observando-se no COpM a gravação de nosso vídeo, não se nota nenhum contato radar positivo semelhante ao reportado por TABA. Todavia, por outro lado, constata-se que houve uma deteção bastante positiva do LP-23 sobre alguma coisa que se deslocava no rumo oeste, com uma velocidade de cerca de 40 nós, sem indicação de altitude. Tal contato teve início na radial 300 a 3MN de Anápolis e terminou na radial 266, a 23MN, havendo uma breve perda por volta das 8MN de AN (radial 250), contato esse que teve uma duração de cerca de 30 minutos.
Houve também um outro contato radar positivo (mas não tão prolongado como o 1º) com outro objeto que também se deslocava no rumo oeste, com velocidade aproximada de 30 nós (observada no Controle Direto). Tal contato teve início na radial 230 de AN a 3MN e terminou na 250, a 5MN.

4th APPEARANCE
On 05 MAY, around 2205P, TABA reported detecting something moving between radials 120 and 270 from Anápolis, with an approximate heading of 270, between 3 and 12 MN from Anápolis depending on the radial it was crossing. When the object crossed the final approach to runway 06, PAR detected it, making it possible to establish that its altitude was 6150 feet.
Reviewing our video recording at COpM, no positive radar contact similar to that reported by TABA is apparent. However, a quite positive LP-23 detection can be seen of something moving west at about 40 knots, without an altitude indication. This contact began on radial 300 at 3MN from Anápolis and ended on radial 266 at 23MN, with a brief loss around 8MN from AN (radial 250); the contact lasted approximately 30 minutes.
There was also another positive radar contact (but not as prolonged as the 1st) with another object also moving west at approximately 30 knots (observed on Direct Control). This contact began on radial 230 from AN at 3MN and ended on radial 250 at 5MN.
Because of TABA's radar contacts (mentioned in the 1st paragraph above), on the following day (06 MAY), an F-103 pilot returning to Anápolis after an Alert mission was asked to conduct a visual search in certain sectors near Anápolis to check for highways, railways or hills in those sectors.
